title: Preparing Small, Live Aiptasia Polyps for Confocal Microscopy
author: OSU Weis Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rigd4bw

steps.title: Prepare Relaxing Solution
steps.instruction: Create a 1:1 solution of regular seawater (filtered/sterile optional) and 0.37M MgCl2.

steps.title: Relax Anemones
steps.instruction: Place anemones in the relaxing solution; they should relax (expand and become unresponsive to touch) within 10 minutes. This can be performed directly on a MatTek glass-bottom culture dish for inverted microscopes.

steps.title: Apply Vital Dyes
steps.instruction: Add fluorescent, vital dyes to the sample during the relaxation step, allowing 30-60 minutes for typical load times.

steps.title: Embed or Position Samples
steps.instruction: Secure the relaxed animals using either a low melting agarose mixture or a small volume of relaxing solution.

substeps.instruction: For agarose embedding: Add a few drops of new relaxing solution mixed with 0.5-1.5% low melting agarose (boiled, then cooled to 28-30°C).
Allow to cool and add liquid media to fill most of the glass-bottom dish (~3mL).
For non-agarose embedding: Add just enough relaxing solution to cover the anemones over the shallow well created by the coverslip circle, ensuring they do not dry out.

steps.title: Recover Adult Anemones
steps.instruction: After imaging, recover adult anemones from the agarose.

substeps.instruction: Remove the agarose surrounding the anemones.
Place the anemones back into seawater.
